## Data Cleaning and Preprocessing

## Drop Unnecessary Columns
>>>>>>> 0fecb38 (Added initial Lightcast data cleaning section)

We removed tracking fields and redundant classification variables where present so that the dataset is easier to interpret and use for analysis.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

columns_to_drop = [
    "ID", "URL", "ACTIVE_URLS", "DUPLICATES", "LAST_UPDATED_TIMESTAMP",
    "NAICS2", "NAICS3", "NAICS4", "NAICS5", "NAICS6",
    "SOC_2", "SOC_3", "SOC_5"
]

df_clean = df.drop(*[c for c in columns_to_drop if c in df.columns])

print("Columns before:", len(df.columns))
print("Columns after:", len(df_clean.columns))

```
We examined missing values to better understand data quality. Since our analysis focuses on salary, industry, and work arrangements, we kept only observations with usable values in key variables.

## Handle missing Values

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

df_clean = df_clean.filter(
    col("SALARY_FROM").isNotNull() &
    col("SALARY_TO").isNotNull() &
    col("TITLE").isNotNull() &
    col("REMOTE_TYPE_NAME").isNotNull() &
    col("NAICS_2022_6_NAME").isNotNull() &
    col("STATE_NAME").isNotNull()
)

print("Rows after filtering:", df_clean.count())
```
We examined missing values to better understand data quality. Since our analysis focuses on salary, industry, and work arrangements, we kept only observations with usable values in key variables. This approach preserves meaningful observations while ensuring that key variables are available for analysis.

## Convert Data Types

We converted posting dates to a date format so that date fields would be interpreted correctly.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

df_clean = df_clean.withColumn(
    "POSTED",
    F.to_date("POSTED", "M/d/yyyy")
)

df_clean.select("POSTED").show(5, truncate=False)
```

## Remove Duplicates
```{python}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

before_rows = df_clean.count()

df_clean = df_clean.dropDuplicates()

after_rows = df_clean.count()

print("Rows before removing duplicates:", before_rows)
print("Rows after removing duplicates:", after_rows)
print("Duplicates removed:", before_rows - after_rows)
```

Duplicate job postings can inflate counts and distort patterns. To prevent double counting, we removed duplicate rows.

## Create Salary Measure
```{python}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

df_clean = df_clean.withColumn(
    "salary_midpoint",
    (col("SALARY_FROM") + col("SALARY_TO")) / 2
)

df_clean = df_clean.filter(col("salary_midpoint") > 0)

df_clean.select("SALARY_FROM", "SALARY_TO", "salary_midpoint").show(5)
```
This helps reduce the complexity of working with salary ranges and allows for easier comparison across job postings.
